scope: Numerical direct-solve and authenticated one-patch F32 feasibility/recovery qualification; no model-value experiment or production activation.
constraint: One joint L2/Frobenius update ball across all output coefficients, around exact F32 anchors; no row-count normalization.
invariants: None preserves the previous unconstrained request-serialization identity and execution semantics.
Some participates in the canonical request commitment.
A zero radius is a singleton; no finite multiplier or general KKT condition is fabricated.
Per-output sample weights may differ; every output shares the same radius multiplier.
F64 stationarity and radius checks are numerical diagnostics, not exact global-optimality certificates.
F32 lowering toward the anchor is independently checked using exact 576-bit integer squared differences against the exact F64 radius square.
F32 feasibility never certifies F32 optimality, held-out quality or task value.
Guard independently recomputes this single patch's budget from expected/replacement bytes; the existing patch path authenticates the complete source SHA and expected bytes.
Repeated addresses, forged source bytes and malformed data cannot be accepted.
The budget excludes separately supplied bias, environment changes and cumulative drift across multiple patches.
Signed-zero numeric difference is zero even when bytes change.
The strict gain > minimum_gain rule and original recovery checks remain in force.

unit_and_file_cases: Scalar active and inactive balls with analytic solutions.
Two differently weighted outputs with nonzero anchors and a known common multiplier.
Zero radius; illegal radii; anchors not exactly representable as F32.
F32 rounding outward at decimal boundaries and inward lowering.
Exact norm boundary and adjacent F64 radii; subnormal updates and extreme radii.
1024 opposite maximum-F32 updates and mixed extreme exponents.
Pre-publication budget rejection, forged expected bytes, repeated indices and zero-gain restoration.
Worst-case multiplier search admitted against the original 80M work cap.
verification.external_rpc: Launch the newly built controller and use its shipped stdio MCP path; record binary and source hashes. Compare the exact norm receipt with Python Fraction and constrained F64 solutions with an independent eigensystem reference.
verification.fixture_precision: Explicitly derive a serialized F32 anchor from the public F64 fixture and lift those exact values to F64 for both solvers; identify the derived fixture separately.
verification.f64_reference_tolerance: max absolute parameter error <= 1e-8*(1+max absolute reference parameter); report multiplier, KKT and objective differences separately.
verification.f32_feasibility: Exact Fraction squared norm <= exact Fraction radius squared; no tolerance and no dropped failing cases.
verification.failures: Retain failed builds, tests, RPC attempts and their costs; corrections require new attempt records.
